laws.rule: Foreign tourists over 12 pay a USD 200 Galápagos protected-areas entry fee on arrival at Baltra or San Cristóbal (USD 100 under 12) and need a USD 20 Transit Control Card bought before flying.

Galápagos National Park and Marine Reserve, article 4(3-6, 11-14): stay on authorised trails/delimited areas; keep at least 2 m from wildlife while walking, snorkelling, diving or freediving, including camera equipment. Kayak, stand-up paddleboard and panga-ride observation require at least 4 m from the coast and observed animals. Boat-based whale/dolphin viewing has separate 100 m/50 m minimums, doubled for groups with young. Do not touch, feed, chase or interfere with wildlife or remove natural material. Observe biosecurity inspections and take all waste out to authorised disposal points. This is protected-area law, not a province-wide blanket ban on ordinary possessions.
The park's visit rules say: do not use drones. Take photos without flash; professional filming needs authorisation.

Galápagos protected areas, article 4(1-3, 10): use a DPNG-accredited and authorised naturalist guide except at sites DPNG has expressly exempted from obligatory accompaniment. Tourism operations/services must be duly authorised. Camping is limited to expressly authorised sites with a prior permit requested at least 48 hours in advance. This does not establish that every settlement, beach or island requires a guide.

Galápagos protected areas, article 4(15): carrying and consuming alcoholic drinks and legally controlled substances are prohibited, as are smoking, electronic smoking/vaping/inhalation devices, campfires and generating fire. Article 4(9) separately prohibits promoting these products using protected-area visitor sites, beaches, infrastructure or landscapes. No province-wide alcohol ban or prescription-medicine exemption/ban is inferred.

The Galápagos Council official TCT FAQ says tourists need a Tarjeta de Control de Tránsito, presented on entry to and exit from the province, current identification or passport, and a personal return air ticket between the mainland and Galápagos. It describes a maximum tourist stay of 60 non-extendable days in the year and says tourist status does not permit income-earning activity. Confirm current documentary requirements with the Council before travel.

Articles 5-6 list prior agency-managed reservations for Fausto Llerena-Ruta de la Tortuga (Santa Cruz), Arnaldo Tupiza (Isabela), David Rodríguez (San Cristóbal), Las Grietas (Santa Cruz), Volcán Chico and Minas de Azufre (Isabela), plus later duly incorporated sites. Read with the October corrected Annex I: tourists/transient visitors at included sites must be on a valid reservation and comply with date/site/time/capacity; the registered guide presents the QR/confirmation. Permanent/temporary residents showing a valid residence card are exempt from reservation, not from hours, entry controls or capacity. No universal island-wide advance-booking rule or guarantee of slots is inferred.

Article 4(7): photographs must be without flash or devices that disturb wildlife; filming and professional photography require prior DPNG authorisation. The precise treatment of casual personal video has not been clarified in this pass. No equipment authorisations or fee amounts inferred.

Article 4(16,19): noisy use of speakers, radios, megaphones, phones or similar playback devices in the natural visitor environment is prohibited; personal headphones are allowed. Aquatic activities restrict sunscreens containing oxybenzone, octinoxate or other compounds potentially harmful to marine ecosystems. This is not a ban on possessing a phone or on all sunscreen; a complete product list is not yet checked.

local-law.note: Primary September 2026 protected-area regulation and October corrected reservation annex read directly. These update the older poster-based wildlife, guide/camping and alcohol entries; the older entry-fee, provincial TCT and aerial-equipment entries retain their own dates and were not rechecked. No charges added or revalidated here. Rules govern the park/reserve and specified visitor sites, not every part of the province. Other local levels and later amendments not yet checked. New detail is from primary 2026 instruments, not a government news story. The corrected October Annex I takes precedence over the September annex for reservation workflow; live site availability and all subsequent amendments not yet checked.

items.text: Galápagos National Park/Marine Reserve protected areas: article 4(15) prohibits carrying and consuming alcoholic drinks. Do not expand this to all provincial settlements or Ecuador.

Galápagos protected areas: article 4(15) prohibits smoking and use of electronic/similar devices to smoke, vaporise or inhale substances. It also prohibits fires. No inference that mere possession of an unused cigarette packet is expressly banned by this clause.

closures: Article 4(18), Galápagos National Park areas: general visits 06:00-18:00. Diving until 17:00; night diving only at sites defined in the relevant rules, 18:00-22:00. DPNG can set specific hours, limit entry or require earlier departure. These are Ecuador/Galápagos site-local clock times, not AEST, and are not a province-wide curfew.
